newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WMC to defer St Ives gold expansion.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WMC to defer St Ives gold expansion.

text.p: WMC Ltd said on Wednesday it was deferring a A$157 million expansion of its St Ives gold mine in Western Australia due to declines in the gold price.

"Since the end of the quarter, there has been a further fall in the price of gold and the market outlook has become uncertain," WMC said in its quarterly production report and shareholders' review for the quarter ended June 30, 1997.
The consequence has been an immediate impact on development plans at St Ives, WMC said. "The A$157 million expansion project will be deferred," WMC said.

Expenses incurred so far of about A$30 million will be offset by closing out some 250,000 ounces of the forward sales specifically entered into to protect the capital exposure to the project, WMC said.
"The existing plant will be repaired and improved at a cost of approximately A$30 million, ensuring ongoing gold output of about 400,000 ounces per annum," WMC said.

World gold prices plummeted to 12-year lows of around US$313 an ounce last week after the Australian central bank said it had sold 167 tonnes of gold reserves over the past six months in favour of foreign currency-backed securities.
Gold has since recovered slightly, although long term, some analysts believe the precious metal is in for a rough ride.
Low inflation forecasts and alternative investment in equities and other paper markets continue to chip away at the price, analysts said.

WMC approved the expansion last November, which mainly involved constructing a new gold processing plant at the mine to initially treat five million tonnes of ore but eventually growing to seven million tonnes.
The expansion was to take St Ives output first to about 500,000 ounces and then 700,000 ounces.
WMC is one of the largest gold miners in Australia. In 1996/97 (July/June), it produced 770,336 ounces of gold, up from 744,552 ounces the previous year, company figures show.
